text: This will also prevent duplicative efforts and ensure that our principles are aligned, while working with individual agencies leading the various initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Some issues that we will need to deal with include, which areas, sectors or population segments are most at risk and how can we further support these groups?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: What additional research is needed for sectors to develop effective, tailored measures?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: How do we balance the need for additional cooling against the need to meet our emission targets?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Office will work with Government agencies to engage businesses and communities on these important issues and explore how we can build heat resilience in our local spaces and communities together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They are practical and worth taking a closer look with the relevant agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will take these onboard as we engage our stakeholders and develop our Action Plan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Coordinated oversight of our research and technology efforts for heat resilience is also needed so that we continue to build capabilities and deepen our knowledge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This ensures that the measures under the Action Plan are backed by science.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will launch the RIE2030 Heat Resilience R&D Programme, to advance capabilities and investments in heat resilience research through two complementary pillars – one focusing on infrastructure interventions and the other on understanding and managing impact of heat on society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr David Hoe asked how our heat resilience plans will cater to vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will be a key area of our research under the new Funding Initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will devote more resources to study and protect those who are more vulnerable to heat, such as the elderly and the very young and those who are more exposed to heat, such as outdoor workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We aim to better understand how heat affects us all, and develop tailored guidelines and solutions to help everyone thrive in a warming world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This new bound of research builds on work that we have done over the years, bringing together researchers and agencies to co-create innovative solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, under the Cooling Singapore 2.0 project, researchers have worked with Government agencies to develop an island-wide Digital Urban Climate Twin to simulate Singapore's urban climate and assess the effectiveness of various cooling strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will guide agencies in testing and implementing heat mitigation strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As we chart out our next bound of research efforts under the RIE2030 Heat Resilience R&D Programme, we call for researchers and industry to join us on this journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Office will also lead international engagements and collaborations on heat resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will share our efforts and learn from other countries' best practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is not new, but will now be more coordinated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For instance, following the success of the Digital Urban Climate Twin by the Singapore-ETH Centre, local authorities in Brazil are piloting the tool to simulate city- and district-level climate change scenarios.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This heat resilience strategy also works alongside existing efforts, such as the Go25 national movement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Launched last year, Go25 encourages behavioural change by getting residents to set the indoor air-conditioning temperature at 25 degrees in their homes, offices and buildings where possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The aim is to tackle overcooling and reduce energy use, without sacrificing thermal comfort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The campaign in 2025 saw strong participation from around 200 industry partners who committed to reduce over-cooling, adopt sustainable practices and build long-term heat resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A win for the environment and long-term cost savings, without compromising on thermal comfort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I encourage Members to visit the common spaces of our integrated hubs, such as Our Tampines Hub and Wisma Geylang Serai, as well as our community clubs, such as Yuhua Community Centre and Kebun Baru Community Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They have pledged to Go25 and installed hybrid cooling systems, which include a combination of fans and air-conditioning, to keep our shared spaces comfortable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As we adapt to climate change, we must also work to mitigate our impact on the environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For households, residents can use vouchers under the Climate Friendly Households Programme to purchase energy and water efficient household appliances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ms Hany Soh asked about our plans for this programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Creating a circular economy is another key enabler of climate mitigation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: By shifting towards mindful consumption and sustainable habits of reducing, reusing and recycling, we can minimise the amount of waste disposed of.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Since launching the Zero Waste Masterplan in 2019, we have introduced segregated recycling to complement mixed recycling through the blue bins.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, we introduced Singapore’s first Extended Producer Responsibility scheme in 2021 to ensure proper end-of-life management and the recycling of e-waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For food waste, the Good Samaritan Food Donation Act, which commenced in 2025, will facilitate the donation of surplus food to beneficiaries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In addition, under the Resource Sustainability Act, new commercial and industrial buildings that generate large amount of food waste are required to segregate them for treatment and reporting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One waste stream that deserves particular attention is packaging waste, of which plastics is a significant component.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The amount of packaging waste generated in Singapore forms one third of our domestic waste generated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is why we are strengthening circularity for packaging.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ms Hany Soh and Ms Lee Hui Ying asked about our efforts to tackle this waste stream.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In July 2023, we implemented the Disposable Carrier Bag Charge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Dennis Tan also asked if we will expand our Extended Producer Responsibility scheme to enhance producer accountability in managing waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We had recently discussed in the House our second EPR, the Beverage Container Return Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In a few weeks, the scheme will launch with the tagline “Return Right”.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Return Right began as a recommendation by a Recycle Right Citizens’ Workgroup in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This House supported legislative changes to enact the scheme in 2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Subsequently, a consortium of producers came together to form BCRS Ltd to operationalise the scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Through Return Right, we hope that Singaporeans will also become more mindful of the packaging they consume, dispose of waste properly to keep our shared spaces clean and practise good recycling habits, which will reduce the contamination in our blue recycling bins.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Return Right would require all of us to make some adjustments – producers, retailers, consumers, food shops and more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Based on the experiences in other countries, it will take time for the scheme to settle into a steady cadence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: While the scheme starts in April, containers bearing the scheme’s deposit mark will gradually enter the market over the transition period, with widespread availability by August and September this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will give everyone some time to transit to a new way of recycling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In the coming weeks, we will expand outreach efforts with partners, scale up online publicity and see materials at stores explaining how the scheme works and where to recycle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to work closely with the industry to ensure transparent pricing for consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are also working with BCRS Ltd to make recycling as practical as possible, while keeping the cost of operations reasonable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Some of these additional RVM locations have already been identified and the remaining ones will be located based on return patterns, and feedback from the community and other stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We recognise that some seniors and persons with disabilities may require additional support to adapt to the scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will therefore work with community partners such as TOUCH Community Services, Tzu-Chi Foundation (Singapore) and the Singapore Environment Council to reach out to these groups, to better help them understand the scheme and address any challenges they may face in returning their beverage containers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are also working with SG Enable to improve the return experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I have spoken about purchasing beverages from the supermarket or a retail shop and returning them at the RVMs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But what happens when we order a beverage while dining outside in a restaurant?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The F&B landscape in Singapore is very diverse, with different settings and operating models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To address this, we have identified two main typologies, which will be clearly differentiated for consumers’ ease.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Some restaurants and food shops have indicated that they plan to collect back the containers of beverages consumed during dining-in and hence they will not charge their customers the 10-cent deposit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These establishments will be known as Return Right F&B outlets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Because they will take care of the beverage containers, they are taking on the responsibility and so, they will not transfer that responsibility on to their customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They will not be charging their customers the 10-cent deposit when you are dining in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They will either serve the beverages in cups or glasses without containers or serve the drinks with the containers, with the understanding that customers leave them behind or at the tray return point after consumption for collection by the outlet.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To help diners easily identify these outlets, they will display signages and decals prominently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For the customer, this arrangement is similar to the current dining experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For restaurants and food shops not participating in the Return Right F&B scheme, the default arrangement will apply – beverage containers will be sold with the 10-cent deposit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In short, the 10-cent deposit follows the container, and the responsibility then to deal with the container and recycle it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This default arrangement is also more suitable for certain settings, such as hawker centres and most coffeeshops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In these settings, takeback arrangements could be quite challenging due to the porous nature of the dining areas and the presence of multiple drink stalls within the same area in the case of hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Most HDB coffeeshops will be within a five-minute walk from an RVM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For hawker centres, which serve as high-footfall community gathering points, an RVM will be placed either within the premises or nearby once the RVMs are fully deployed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Recycling is a shared responsibility, and everyone has a role to play.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We can each do our part in making beverage container return work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But every small effort counts, and together, we can build a greener and more sustainable Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The spirit of shared responsibility and collective action must extend to how we take care of our common spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To address persistent feedback on high-rise littering, NEA is piloting an enhanced partnership with Town Councils.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These measures are supplemented by targeted enforcement, including more than 900 thermal camera deployments in HDB common areas with persistent feedback since 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These cameras effectively detected smoking offences in about 44% of deployments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: On vector control, NEA has tightened its enforcement against rat-related lapses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: NEA will also continue to support effective vector control, working with stakeholders to raise service standards and enhancing capabilities through training and information sharing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Relying on regulations and enforcement alone is not enough.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Collective effort by the community remains critical in helping us safeguard public health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Smokers should be considerate of those around them when they smoke.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Premises owners and residents have a responsibility to prevent mosquito breeding and rat infestation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, climate adaptation requires a collective effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As we chart our next-bound efforts in strengthening our water, heat and resource resilience, everyone can play their part.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is a vision for today and for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Everyone, from Government to industry to the community, can help build a liveable Singapore today and for many years to come.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, I will speak on our approach to strengthen food resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As a country heavily reliant on imports, we are particularly vulnerable to external shocks and supply chain disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Over the past five years, Singapore's food supply has been repeatedly tested by events beyond our control.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: During COVID-19, there were concerns that countries' COVID-19 measures would lead to food supply disruptions, such as eggs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In 2022, Malaysia's ban on the export of live chickens disrupted their supply to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: More recently, the disruption in pork supply from Bulan, Indonesia in 2023, due to an African Swine Fever outbreak, further highlighted our vulnerabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Each time, we managed to tide through the disruption with the collective support of our importers, retailers and consumers who switched to alternative options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We must stay prepared for rising geopolitical tensions and trade restrictions which could disrupt our food supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The latest chain of events in the Middle East only underscores this global climate of uncertainty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We also need to manage our risks from animal diseases, which add to further pressure on global food supply and global prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As a long-term risk, we must be able to adapt to climate change, such as extreme and erratic weather which affects crop yields globally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is why we need to build options and flexibility to deal with the different types of disruptions – whether they affect single or multiple food items, single sources or entire regions, and whether they last for days or they last for months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have learnt many lessons from our "30 by 30" initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: While it had successfully catalysed local production growth, mainly focusing on one pillar – Grow Local – left us vulnerable to the very disruptions that we sought to address.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These enable us to tap onto the different combinations to address different types of scenarios and that will strengthen our food resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But first, what does it mean to achieve "food resilience"?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It will not always be possible to have everyone's favourite food and brand available in every disruption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But we will prioritise staples such as rice, proteins and vegetables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And like any insurance policy, we must be strategic about what we protect and how we protect it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This approach allows us to provide food assurance where it matters most, whilst managing our risks responsibly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The first food pillar is for industry to diversify imports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This means importing our food from multiple sources and building up alternative sources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Doing so reduces the impact when there are disruptions to particular sources, helping us to stabilise our food supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And also, it makes easier to pivot to alternative sources when needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: When disease outbreaks happen, we do not shut down supply from entire countries – we get more precise these days.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our regionalisation agreements allow us to continue importing from disease-free areas within affected countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, during Brazil's Avian Influenza outbreak last year, we maintained poultry imports from accredited farms in unaffected regions, rather than restricting imports from the whole of Brazil.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will continue to facilitate accreditation and explore regionalisation arrangements with suitable sources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Diversification alone is not enough and has its constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, importers may need to buy from sources that are not necessarily the cheapest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, we have to also strengthen the resilience of existing food supply chains by working with like-minded countries and regions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is where global partnerships, our newest pillar, comes in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Ng Shi Xuan asked how we assess whether our global partnerships can support diversification.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As shared in Parliament last month, partnerships can take various forms, such as facilitating production overseas, in addition to having government-to-government arrangements and agreements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For such partnerships to be meaningful and sustainable, they must be win-win.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And this will look different for various partnerships.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These help us ensure a stable rice supply to Singapore and provide an avenue for Singapore to activate additional rice supplies when needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The joint study with Brunei on the feasibility of an Agri-Tech Food Zone in Brunei will explore how both countries can leverage on our respective strengths to enhance agri-food trade and food supply resilience, starting with aquaculture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: When the next disruption hits, we do not want to be scrambling for alternatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We want to have pre-established channels, we want to have tested protocols and trusted partners who are ready to respond.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This transforms crisis management from reactive scrambling to proactive deployment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will continue to explore mutually beneficial arrangements with like-minded economies to strengthen our food supply resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, even with our efforts to reduce the likelihood and impact of disruptions, it is still possible that we could face widespread disruptions where food cannot reach our borders for some time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And this is why we will stockpile essential food items, such as rice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It gives us the time and breathing space to restore our food flows and sustain our population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will continue to work with the industry to stockpile more effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Grow local remains an important pillar of our food resilience strategy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Stockpiles are finite and imports can be disrupted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Local farms can provide us with a regenerative source of fresh food, that is maintained even during prolonged disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: More of our farms are moving towards controlled environments which makes them more climate-resilient and land-efficient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Poh Li San asked about the lessons learnt from failed local farms and Mr Ng Shi Xuan asked about Singapore's role in alternative proteins.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We must first recognise that most of our farming industry is nascent and in an early phase of growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It will take them time to develop viable technologies and business models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We must also take a practical approach on what we can grow locally in a sustainable manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These goals take into account the strengths of our local farming ecosystem and the potential for growth in supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have also got to be realistic about our economics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our local farms will always face higher land and production costs compared to farms from the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But the situation is no different from how Singapore differentiates from low-cost alternatives in other industries, such as manufacturing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have to improve our value-add, bring higher-productivity and cost-efficiency, and with Government's support to invest in capability and capacity development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But here is what we have also learnt on the demand side: consumers and large buyers, like supermarkets, are willing to pay a reasonable premium for fresher, pesticide-free local produce that comes with guaranteed supply certainty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: What this means is that they want consistent supply at scale.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, the key is thus to get our farms to the right scale and cost structure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It has achieved this balance, with local production making up to 30% of local consumption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Lee Hui Ying and Mr Cai Yinzhou asked how we will support and promote awareness of our local farms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are helping farms to increase productivity and reap economies of scale, we are helping them to build capabilities, strengthen supply resilience of agri-inputs and enhance demand offtake.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The first tranche of the Agri-food Cluster Transformation (ACT) Fund, launched in 2021, has shown that Singapore farms can transform into advanced farming operations that are of higher yield, that are more pest- and disease- resilient, and increasingly climate-resilient too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Fund has enabled both agri- and aqua-farms to adopt everything from simple, small-scale technologies, like LED grow lights, automated feeders and automated irrigation systems that reduce manual labour, to large-scale farming systems in climate-controlled environments that guarantee year-round production regardless of the weather.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Take Singapore Aquaculture Technology as a good example of this transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Using ACT Fund support, instead of adopting conventional open cage fish farm technologies, they deployed a closed containment aquaculture system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They now operate at three times the productivity of conventional sea-based fish farms and in using closed containment aquaculture system, they face lower risk from environmental hazards, such as algal blooms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Closed containment aquaculture system technology is still nascent and requires industry readiness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Thus, to Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin's question, it will take time for the local industry to adopt systems such as closed containment aquaculture system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Singapore Food Agency (SFA) will continue to support farms who are keen and ready for this transition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Another beneficiary of the ACT Fund is Yili Farm who upgraded their cultivation systems to optimise layout, improve crop protection and integrate with their centralised nursery and irrigation system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This enabled faster crop cycles and a 20% increase in productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These developments give us confidence to enhance the Fund to support our farms further.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This will be made available from April 2026, over five years, and it represents our largest industry scheme to date to support technology adoption and local agriculture capability and capacity building.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is in response to feedback from the industry on the need for collaborative approaches to tackle common challenges, such as limited economies of scale and supply chain inefficiencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This new scheme will co-fund strategic partnerships between farms and ecosystem players on the development and deployment of industry-wide solutions that can support multiple farms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Examples will include farms and industry players collaborating on integrated delivery systems which streamlines the process from farm-to-market, reducing transportation cost and improving product freshness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For the aquaculture sector, we will also support both sea-based and land-based farms to adopt newer technologies to improve productivity and consistency of output through demonstration projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One example is the automated vaccination of fingerlings which can reduce labour intensity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Successfully demonstrated technologies can subsequently be adopted by the industry via the ACT Fund 2.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Beyond technology, quality agri-inputs, such as eggs, fingerlings and feed, are fundamental to success for aquaculture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, farms source a majority of their fry and fingerling from overseas sources with less consistent quality and lower survival rates due to the long transport stress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The National Broodstock Centre produces disease-free broodstock that commercial hatcheries then develop into high quality fingerlings under strict biosecurity standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For farms, this translates directly into better profitability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These premium fingerlings grow faster, survive better and they convert feed more efficiently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: That means that farms reach market quicker with lower feed costs and fewer losses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We started out with Asian Seabass and have since successfully expanded into Marine Tilapia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: High-quality eggs and fingerlings set the foundation, but health and nutrition inputs determine whether farms achieve optimal growth and disease resistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SFA's new Integrated Hatchery Support Programme will help local hatcheries adopt specialised feeds and quality vaccines that maximise the growth potential of the high quality fries or fingerlings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And this will be done through demonstration trials to build farm's confidence in investing in better quality input.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Together, the National Broodstock Centre, Hatchery Development and Recognition Programme and Integrated Hatchery Support Programme create a reinforced aquaculture value chain for both sea-based and land-based farms that improve fry quality, increase yields and sharpen competitiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our offtake programmes have been making progress for the food types that matter most to Singapore's food resilience – and we aim to do better.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Central to this effort is the Singapore Agro-Food Enterprises Federation (SAFEF), which has become the critical demand aggregation engine that matches our farms' production capacity with local needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked about the effectiveness of SAFEF's demand aggregation efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SAFEF has created sustainable brands like "The Straits Fish" and "SG Farmers' Market" now stocked in major supermarkets – FairPrice, Sheng Siong, Cold Storage and Giant, bringing local produce closer to the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are expanding the demand aggregation model in 2026 with more product varieties and The Straits Fish marine tilapia ready-to-eat products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SAFEF will also partner more food and beverage (F&B) players to integrate SG Farmers' Market® product range in their menus.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This effort aims to facilitate farms’ mainstream market penetration by connecting retail demands with a fragmented local farm supply chain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And this is just due to our small agriculture sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In aggregated offtake programmes, we give farms the sales certainty they need to scale production.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: At the same time, supermarkets, hotels and caterers are given the confidence in a guaranteed reliable local supply for them to commit shelf space and marketing support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The effectiveness of our Singapore Food Story also depends on our readiness to respond swiftly to disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: SFA is strengthening early warning systems to provide greater lead time for action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our new risk monitoring dashboard and food supply visibility tool, developed with PSA BDP, provides early warnings of developments that may affect food imports and strengthens Singapore's upstream food supply chain visibility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This tool has already proven its value – it expedited our risk assessments during Brazil's Avian Influenza outbreaks in May last year and the recent conflict in the Middle East.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Together, these initiatives strengthen SFA's ability to assess, plan and mitigate supply disruption risks before they impact Singapore's food resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Strong supply chain logistics are indeed a critical backbone for resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will continue to work closely with relevant agencies and industry, including to consider your suggestions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, building Singapore's food resilience requires all of us to move beyond individual interests and act with collective urgency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But we cannot secure our food future alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I hope that businesses do more to support our local food production and our overall Singapore Food Story 2 efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Diversify your supply sources and commit to local production as a strategic buffer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: When you choose local suppliers, you are helping to invest in Singapore's food resilience that will protect your business during the next major disruption or major pandemic scenario.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For consumers, your choices shape our collective resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, our founding fathers understood that Singapore's survival depends on collective action over individual interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As our founding Prime Minister often said, we must leave nothing to chance when it comes to Singapore's survival.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, we apply that same principle to food resilience with the Singapore Food Story 2 – building comprehensive resilience through collective action, because our food future is too important to leave to chance alone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Mr Chairman, climate adaptation can sound distant – something handled somewhere else by someone else.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: But in truth, it shows up in everyday life through the sudden downpour that disrupts your commute or the heat that lingers in your flat a little too long after sunset.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: These small but growing inconveniences tell us something important: the environment around us is changing and how we respond will shape how we live.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: In simple terms, climate adaptation means getting ready for disruptions we know are coming.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: How can we help ourselves stay comfortable and stay safe as the climate shifts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: For Singapore, this work is becoming more urgent.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: A year to increase awareness and bring everyone into the action.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: At MSE, this reflects our unified approach to "we first".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Everyone has a stake in how Singapore adapts and everyone has a role in making it work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Over the next few minutes, I will share how we are bringing this approach to life along our coasts, across our communities and in our daily action.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: First, as a land scarce country, Singapore is vulnerable to rising seas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: In simple terms, if we do nothing, each rise in sea level means less land for us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: In January this year, spring tides flooded parts of East Coast Park, even without rain.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: This shows us that coastal flooding is not a distant future problem, it is happening now.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: At its core, coastal protection is about safeguarding land while supporting the way people and nature share our coasts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We see this in Singapore, where steel and concrete abut wilderness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: I saw it myself when I joined a few nature group volunteers on an intertidal walk.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Sea creatures like nudibranchs and sand dollars, right next to Tanah Merah ferry terminal.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We are speaking to communities about coastal protection measures and how they could be designed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: This includes residents, businesses, researchers and nature groups, who all interact with our coast differently, yet care about it deeply.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: I attended one of these sessions at Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve, discussing coastal protection around mangrove habitats.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The conversation was rich of perspectives, discussing trade-offs and exploring how we might combine coastal protection measures with public spaces.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: One suggestion that emerged was transforming the Kranji Tidal Gatehouse into a viewing deck.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We are listening and we are onboarding these views as we develop our coastal protection measures across Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Because when people help shapes what protects them, protection becomes something shared rather than something imposed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Second, with extreme weather events happening more often, I am very sure everyone has been caught in unexpected heavy storms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We continue upgrading our drains and infrastructure, but no city can plan and build its way out of every possible storm.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: For true resilience, we must all be empowered to protect ourselves.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: As Ms Poh Li San highlighted, businesses can take a step to protect their premises from flooding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The Guidebook will be launched in mid-2026 on PUB's website.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: It will help business owners assess their flood exposure through a Do-It-Yourself (DIY) Flood Risk Matrix and decide what protection measures they need for their properties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The guidance is practical and draws directly from industry experience.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Beyond what businesses can do, preparedness starts with each one of us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Look out for PUB's "Get Flood-wise in a F.L.A.S.H." campaign or join their outreach events.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Learn simple actions to keep yourself and your family safe during heavy rains or floods.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Ms Nadia would be glad that we are bringing preparedness to your doorstep.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Join us and act now by subscribing to PUB's flood alerts on Telegram, X or on the MyENV app.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Next, coastal and flood protection are important to keeping Singapore safe and liveable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: An engaged community is what truly makes the difference.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We are encouraged to see communities across Singapore coming forward, coming together with solutions to protect our environment and promote sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We are supporting your efforts through the SG Eco Fund.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Since 2020, the SG Eco Fund has awarded over $21 million to support close to 500 initiatives, engaging over 700,000 individuals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: I am particularly excited about an SG Eco Fund project tackling indoor heat for seniors, a topic less understood and not talked about enough.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: HeatAware SG by Sustainable Living Lab puts sensors in homes to help seniors understand temperature build-up and gives timely cooling advice.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: One senior who they worked with had never used fans, even on hot days, a habit brought over from kampong days.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: But imagine, with rising temperatures, this risks heat stroke.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: With simple monitoring and gentle prompts, seniors are now empowered with the information they need to stay safe when it gets too hot.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Ultimately, to adapt, we must first see clearly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: When we understand what is changing around us, we can prepare.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Ms Hany Soh asked about expanding the SG Eco Fund's scope to support more ground-up action.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: As climate risks grow, we need more focussed action.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: That is why I am announcing the Climate Adaptation Package under the SG Eco Fund.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: But we believe you can make a difference.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: If you have ideas, take advantage of the SG Eco Fund.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We want to hear from you and we are here to support you to turn your ideas into reality.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: To our young people, your energy and your ideas are exactly what we need to build a resilient Singapore, one that you can inherit with confidence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Mr Lee Hong Chuang would be heartened to know that we are also committed to empowering our young people in building resilience beyond our shores.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The National Youth Council's Singapore-Association of Southeast Asia Nations (ASEAN) Youth Fund supports youth sustainability projects across Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: They can also volunteer in sustainability projects overseas through the Youth Corps Expedition Project.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: (In Mandarin):   Singapore is facing severe challenges brought about by climate change.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We must seek better solutions to adapt to these changes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: MSE hopes to encourage all sectors of society to work together with us to make sustainability a part of our daily lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The Beverage Container Return Scheme that Dr Janil Puthucheary mentioned yesterday is a good example.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: To help consumers adapt to the scheme, local major supermarkets will uniformly adopt the following practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The prices displayed on shelves will not include the 10-cent deposit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Supermarkets will clearly inform consumers that they need to pay an additional 10-cent deposit at checkout.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We will continue to work with them to ensure that pricing for bottled and canned beverages remain clear and transparent.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: After finishing the drinks, consumers can put the marked containers into reverse vending machines to retrieve the 10-cent deposit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: SimplyGo EZ-Link cards and concession cards or DBS PayLah! can be used to retrieve the deposit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The new scheme will not only increase the recycling rates of beverage containers but also encourage Singaporeans to develop good recycling habits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Before launching BCRS, we consulted F&B operators extensively and identified two feasible approaches for recycling containers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The first approach is to pour canned beverages into cups for customers to enjoy or to collect the container after consumers finish their drinks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: In such cases, F&B operators will not charge customers the 10-cent deposit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We will classify this category of operators as "Return Right F&B" merchants.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: These F&B operators will display notices in their stores to inform customers that they will not be charged a deposit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: We understand that operators who choose to collect the containers themselves need to put in more effort to modify their work processes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Operators can submit their applications to the National Environment Agency (NEA).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The second approach is to charge customers who purchase canned beverages a 10-cent deposit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: After finishing their drinks, customers can put the container into any reverse vending machine to retrieve their 10-cent deposit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: This model will be more practical for most coffee shop and hawker centre stall owners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Implementing and perfecting a new policy takes time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: During this transition period, we seek the public's support and understanding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: At the same time, we also welcome feedback and suggestions for our reference and improvement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: As long as we work together, we can all do our part to protect the environment. : Mr Chairman, climate adaptation is about preparing early and acting together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: From coasts to floods to community action, each effort depends on all of us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: This is how nations endure, by adapting together, preparing early and building for generations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: The Government will continue investing for the long-term and we invite every Singaporean to be part of this effort.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
text: Because that is what "we first" means – a shared responsibility for a shared future.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: I have a question for Senior Minister of State Dr Janil.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: I highlighted the expensive irony of food waste in Singapore and asked for MSE's plans and efforts to reduce food waste, and in his reply, Dr Janil mentioned only the Good Samaritan Food Donation Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We do indeed want to improve our food waste management and encourage all the stakeholders involved to participate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have, as Ms Poh has highlighted, a number of mechanisms and platforms, as well as legislation in place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We would like to make sure those are fully utilised and continue to work with stakeholders to then study how we can improve the processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: At the moment, we are focusing, in the news and in the House on other waste streams – plastics and packaging – but indeed, food waste is something that we do need to think very seriously about because of the opportunity that it presents in terms of reducing our wastage, improving our resource recycling and reducing the amount that is diverted towards waste and landfill.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The first is in relation to the Beverage Container Return Scheme.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I understand from Senior Minister of State Dr Janil's speech yesterday that the "Return Right" F&B outlets will be given a specific decal to inform consumers about their plans.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In this regard, I wish to ask whether the decals have already been distributed to all of these stakeholders and are we looking at implementing it by 1 April as well?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And to further avoid any confusion among the patrons in the F&B outlets, can we explore having a centralised compiled list of these vendors and perhaps put it on MyENV app?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In this aspect, can I check whether we have also been keeping track in terms of the amount of the waste or energy and water resources that we have conserved through rolling out of this initiative through the SG Eco Funds?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As I mentioned in my speech, it is important to actually measure to manage the outcomes.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The decals are available if the F&B outlets sign up to be part of the "Return Right" F&B scheme.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I would not want Members to think that this has to be done by 1 April.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Whoever has the container then has the responsibility to deal with it.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will be distributing them to outlets that sign up, either before 1 April or after.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The idea of a centralised list is something we can certainly look at and consider.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: To Ms Hany Soh's question about whether we measure the outcomes of SG Eco Fund.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: Today, we do not measure the outcomes in terms of the way that the Member has described, in terms of waste reduced or energy saved.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: However, we do track in terms of the number of applicants that come forward, the profile of the applicants and the quality of the projects that we get.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: This is mainly because the SG Eco Fund was started with the objective of empowering and to increase awareness of sustainability objectives.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: However, over time, as the fund evolves and matures, we could consider.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr David Hoe, for your two cuts and seven minutes.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The first is regarding the how of the climate adaptation plan, and second is about the Beverage Container Return Scheme.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: The Minister mentioned yesterday that heat advisories will be sent out through the myENV app.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: I think that is really useful because most of us have a smart phone today.

text: Yesterday, what I did was, after Parliament, I went to meet my grassroot leaders, in a room of more than 40 grassroot leaders, and I shared this with my grassroot leaders.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
