speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Hoe, can you get to your clarification?

speaker: Mr David Hoe
text: My question is whether the app itself has a multilingual feature so that our seniors or those who are not fully competent in English will be able to use this app.

speaker: Mr David Hoe
text: On the second question regarding the Beverage Container Return Scheme, I am supportive of the recycling efforts and the deployment of 1,000 reverse vending machines (RVMs).

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will also be looking at the usage patterns of the first 1,000 to help us understand where we would locate them.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Obviously, I think that is a lot more that we can do and we should encourage more Singaporeans to download it.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The issues that Mr Hoe has mentioned about language accessibility is precisely what we like to hear from you during this engagement over the Year of Climate Adaptation.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Also, I would like to put on record my thanks to many Members who have given us very well thought-through, considered suggestions on how we should improve the heat resilience of the country.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I think that these will be gold nuggets that we could incorporate into our adaptation plan.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Lee Hui Ying, your three cuts in six minutes.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I just have two quick clarifications for Senior Minister of State Janil.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: First, regarding the pilot that NEA is going through with the Town Councils on the surveillance camera deployments.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Can I get further granular details in terms of the length of this pilot that is ongoing?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: How are these locations being identified for surveillance camera deployment?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I note the additional smoking prohibitions that are in place.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I am just wondering whether NEA could consider AI-enabled technology to be used, especially on smoke detection as well.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is a pilot to see how well this can work, but the intent is to make sure that, in working in partnership with the Town Councils, we increase the responsiveness to ground feedback and shorten the time cycle, increase the speed of the deployment and the potential enforcement action.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: Just two quick remarks on my food resilience points.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: The first being that I thank Senior Minister of State Zaqy for framing it from global partnerships to trusted partnerships.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: Will the Ministry consider giving us a report card on how these global partnerships have been different from our diversifying imports strategy besides going into specific details.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: Can the Ministry make a commitment to make sure that our plant-based protein and alternative protein scene will somehow make its way back into the Singapore Food Story in the future, as I note that the National University of Singapore has some successful cases where they have created viable products for us?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On alternative proteins, that is still in play.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Although today, the market demand is not where one would have thought it would be, so there is a bit of challenge for those who are producing alternative proteins.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But the Member is also right, that there are some who have pivoted to providing alternative proteins in other forms.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We are still continuing to fund research and development (R&D) costs for a number of these outfits out here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We are seeing companies increasingly adopting, for example, business-to-business (B2B) partnership models rather than going to just market independently their own product.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To give some examples, they work with food corporates to allow some of these startups to leverage existing manufacturing, distribution and brand capabilities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, they also provide cell-based seafood cultivation platforms like Umami Bioworks.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: They developed a joint-production agreement with the Japanese seafood producer Maruha Nichiro to develop and commercialise cell-cultivated tuna.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, it is not that they are not viable or not feasible, just that cost-wise, I think the market is not yet ready for this at full scale.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I think there is certainly potential and we will continue to support.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On the Member's other question, which was on global partnerships, this is at a very nascent stage.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As I have shared, we have only started signing some of these agreements last year.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, it is an evolution beyond just what we used to call "grow overseas".

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Right now, with partnerships, you have a variety of things that you can do: government-to-government agreements.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Some parts of it, like with Brunei, we are exploring how we could look at growing aquaculture, for example, as I mentioned in my speech; and with New Zealand, there are other types of agreements that we put in place.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I think the global partnerships today allow us to do different things with different like-minded economies that will help us build our food resilience in times of crisis.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But do give us a bit of time because this is fairly nascent and new, but certainly, we will make a report when the time comes.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Mr Chairman, I just seek a response from the Ministry on my cut on supporting our Pioneer hawkers.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Foo for his clarification and I appreciate his engagement with our Pioneer hawkers in his constituency, which is an extremely important segment of our culture.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: This move was carefully considered to help ease manpower challenges while also preserving the local identity and heritage, and the complexion of our hawker centre and our hawker culture.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: We will monitor the impact because this is a very recent move and we will contemplate further moves if necessary.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The first is regarding food resilience and the initial plans for the Lim Chu Kang Agri-District.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Could the Minister of State please elaborate on that.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The second, I am very glad to hear of the top-up to the ACT Fund.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Does the Ministry track progress and utility of the funds dispersed and are there details of project closures or unsuccessful projects once disbursed?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am glad to hear about the plans to build community resilience.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Could the Senior Parliamentary Secretary please elaborate, beyond the PUB SMS alert service, are there emergency rescue and evacuation drills that the PUB intends to carry out?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Nonetheless, we are still hard at work on it, with inter-agency planning, to look at how we can better optimise the land use, infrastructure needs as well as environmental considerations of how we can get this done a lot better.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: At the same time, it is important that as we do master-planning, it is not just about infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: There are also market aspects that we need to consider, such as market-sensing, technical studies, developing new concepts and ideas.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: You do not want just to build farms as you see them today, but farms of tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We are looking at, for example, multi-tenanted facilities that can make better use of shared services to help our farms survive, build more climate resilient facilities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This puts us on the map for new developments in future that we can also consolidate.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Also, I spoke about how we are looking at integrating some of the things like logistics, supply chain management.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That, I think helps optimise land use and certainly facilities and shared services for our companies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In the meantime, I assure Members that our plans are still in play.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For farms that need land, we are still providing our land use tenders, so, those will still continue.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Our ACT Fund, as I have announced, has just been expanded and enhanced.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Thus far, the numbers that have folded are very small – I think only about two out of 60, so that is about a 3% failure rate.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For the most of it, we are seeing most of these farms providing higher yields, better production levels and producing what we need locally.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I assure Members that we are constantly tracking and doing our best to support our local farms.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: This brings the information directly to our citizens.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: In terms of emergency evacuation drills, PUB has been partnering with different communities.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: For example, I attended a session together with one of the Residents' Networks and Community Emergency and Engagement, that they organised to bring together citizens or their residents to understand what kind of plans should they put in place for their unique locales' needs; and from there, to generate and to create their own way of supporting their own neighbours and friends during a flood incident.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: We are hoping to go out there and partner with more communities to activate them and to get them thinking about what to do during an emergency.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Pritam Singh, even though you filed a very short cut, you have been putting up your hand persistently.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In my cut, I asked about the metrics NEA uses to determine whether appointed public waste collectors should increase the frequency of collection from the larger recycling bins.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I do not believe I heard a reply from Senior Minister of State Janil on that.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, those are the metrics that we track.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
